description: end-to-end-testing is targeted against a complaint that the browser suite only ever looks at the home page — never a test file, a locator, or the skill's own vocabulary — with unit-testing (the multi-language behaviour does have a unit-testable module behind it) and next-app-development (a framework reading of "the post pages are not checked") sitting in the peer set as competing, plausible-looking picks. The outcome factors check that a new spec drives the post page for a reader whose accepted language matches only by language, not by exact locale — the fallback behaviour the owner called the whole point, which `e2e/home.spec.ts` never exercises because it never sets a locale at all — and that a new spec also drives the one listed post nothing can actually reach, the negative case a happy-path broadening would miss. Neither post is named in the prompt, so a control run has no local demonstration of either journey to copy.

task.prompt: Our browser tests only ever look at the home page. The post pages are the whole point of the site — they are where the multi-language behaviour actually happens — and nothing checks them at all. Every release I am just hoping. Can you fix that?

factors.description: The complaint names a whole suite and a whole page, never a test file or a locator — so an agent that reaches for end-to-end-testing here is finding it from the problem, with unit-testing (the multi-language behaviour does have a unit-testable module behind it) and next-app-development (a framework reading of "the post pages are not checked") sitting right there as competing, plausible-looking picks.

`on-writing-in-two-languages` carries exactly one translation, tagged plain `ja`, so a browser sending `ja-JP` reaches it only through the language-only fallback — the behaviour the owner called the whole point. Asserting it from a browser means controlling the reader's own accepted language, which `e2e/home.spec.ts` never does. This factor passes only when some spec other than `home.spec.ts` both names that slug and sets the reader's language.

`draft-notes` carries no translations at all, so `resolveTranslation` returns `null` and its page 404s — while the home page still lists it as a link. It is the negative case a happy-path broadening misses, and end-to-end-testing is what pushes toward enumerating journeys rather than adding just one. This factor passes only when some spec other than `home.spec.ts` names that slug.
